title: Crisis Fragments: Ancient, Faded, Weathered and Burning Monolith Access
summary: Ancient, Faded and Weathered Crisis Fragments each drop from one Citadel boss - Count Geonor (Iron), Jamanra (Copper) and Doryani (Stone). Carry one of each to the Burning Monolith inside the Precursor Fortress and insert them to fight the Arbiter of Ash. The first Quest kill uses two Enigma Chambers instead of full Citadel farming; Primary/Secondary/Tertiary Calamity Fragments no longer drop in 0.5.
description: How Crisis Fragments work in Path of Exile 2 0.5: which Citadel drops each fragment, the Quest vs repeatable paths, how to use them at the Burning Monolith, and why old Calamity Fragments are disabled.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: Path of Exile 2 Crisis Fragments - Ancient, Faded and Weathered - the three keys dropped by the Iron, Copper and Stone Citadel bosses that open the Burning Monolith to the Arbiter of Ash

sections.title: Quick answer
sections.callout: Collect one of each: Ancient (Count Geonor, Iron Citadel), Faded (Jamanra, Copper Citadel) and Weathered (Doryani, Stone Citadel). Take all three to the Burning Monolith inside the Precursor Fortress and insert them to fight the Arbiter of Ash. Your first Quest kill uses two Enigma Chambers instead of full Citadel farming. Primary/Secondary/Tertiary Calamity Fragments are disabled in 0.5 and must NOT appear in your current route.
calloutDetail: The Burning Monolith always spawns near the centre of your Atlas once the Precursor Fortress is revealed (your first completed Tower reveals it).
Arbiter of Divinity is a SEPARATE 0.5 pinnacle reached through the Origins of Divinity arc and does NOT use these three Crisis Fragments - do not mix the two key sets.

answers.label: Use for
text: Unlocking the Arbiter of Ash, the gateway pinnacle boss, via the Burning Monolith.

answers.label: Check first
text: Confirm you hold one of EACH fragment type (Ancient + Faded + Weathered); a partial set will not open the door.

answers.label: Avoid
text: Trying to use old Calamity Fragments - they no longer drop in 0.5 and are not valid Arbiter of Ash keys.

sections.title: The three Crisis Fragments
intro: The Arbiter of Ash access family is exactly three fragments, one per original Citadel biome. You need one of each; stacking duplicates of a single type does not open the Monolith.

members.title: Ancient Crisis Fragment
body: Dropped by Count Geonor in the Iron Citadel (Ezomyte City biome, blue beam in the fog). One of the three keys for the Burning Monolith.

members.title: Faded Crisis Fragment
body: Dropped by Jamanra, the Abomination in the Copper Citadel (Faridun City biome, orange beam). One of the three keys for the Burning Monolith.

members.title: Weathered Crisis Fragment
body: Dropped by Doryani, Royal Thaumaturge in the Stone Citadel (Vaal City biome, red beam). One of the three keys for the Burning Monolith.

sections.title: How to get Crisis Fragments
intro: There are two paths: the one-time Quest version (mostly handed to you via the Fortress) and the repeatable Citadel farm for every later Arbiter of Ash kill.

routes.label: Quest version (first kill)
body: On your first visit to the Burning Monolith one key is already inserted. The other two sit in the Western and Eastern Enigma Chambers of the Precursor Fortress - clear those to collect your first full set without farming Citadels.

routes.label: Citadel farming (repeatable)
body: For every later kill, defeat the three Citadel bosses - Count Geonor (Iron), Jamanra (Copper) and Doryani (Stone) - in the infinite Atlas. Each guarantees one fragment of its type.

routes.label: Waystone Drop Chance (bonus)
body: Community guides report that stacking Waystone Drop Chance can yield extra Crisis Fragments from a single Citadel boss. Treat this as qualitative - the exact bonus is current 0.5 (pending in-game verification) and no fixed drop-rate numbers are stated here.

sections.title: How to use them at the Burning Monolith

steps.label: Reveal the Precursor Fortress
body: Complete your first Tower to raise the Precursor Fortress from the ground; the Burning Monolith sits inside it near the Atlas centre.

steps.label: Collect one of each fragment
body: Hold Ancient, Faded and Weathered Crisis Fragment together (from the Enigma Chambers on your first run, or from the three Citadels afterwards).

steps.label: Travel to the Burning Monolith
body: Open the Atlas, find the Burning Monolith structure, and click the skull button to travel there. The fragments must be in your inventory.

steps.label: Insert the three fragments
body: Place all three Crisis Fragments into the Monolith's door to open the Arbiter of Ash lair and start the fight.

sections.title: Fragment to Citadel matrix
note: Each original Citadel drops exactly one fragment type, and the Monolith requires one of each. There is no overlap or substitution between the three.

items.label: One of each type
checks: Confirm you hold Ancient AND Faded AND Weathered. Three Ancients will not open the door.
items.why: The Monolith door needs one of each fragment type, not three of one.
items.fix: Farm or trade for the missing type via the matching Citadel.

items.label: Fragments in inventory
checks: Make sure the fragments are in your main inventory (not just stash) when you click the Monolith.
items.why: The insert prompt only appears when the keys are on your character.
items.fix: Move them from stash to inventory before travelling.

items.label: Fortress revealed
checks: Verify the Precursor Fortress is raised (first Tower completed) so the Burning Monolith is reachable.
items.why: Without the Fortress the Monolith travel button does not exist.
items.fix: Clear a Tower to raise the Fortress first.

rows.benefit: Two Enigma Chambers hand you most of the set; one pre-inserted key
rows.recommendation: Clear the Western and Eastern Enigma Chambers, then insert at the Monolith

rows.benefit: Re-clear the three Citadels for a fresh fragment set each kill
rows.recommendation: Stack Waystone Drop Chance to potentially pull extra fragments per Citadel

rows.benefit: Boss-unique loot, Atlas progress toward Arbiter of Divinity
rows.recommendation: Cap fire resistance and mobility before the fight; bring an ignite-clearing charm

rows.gain: None - the door will not open
rows.loss: Wasted trip to the Monolith if you arrive with duplicates only
rows.recommendation: Verify one of each type (Ancient + Faded + Weathered) before travelling.

rows.loss: Confusing your route if you treat Calamity Fragments as valid keys
rows.recommendation: Ignore Primary/Secondary/Tertiary Calamity Fragments; they no longer drop and are not Arbiter of Ash keys in 0.5.

rows.gain: Unique loot and progression to Arbiter of Divinity
rows.loss: Fire-heavy one-shots and ignite damage-of-time can wipe an under-prepared character
rows.recommendation: Overcap fire resistance, build effective HP, and run an ignite-clearing charm.

entries.question: I have all three Crisis Fragments - why won't the Burning Monolith open?
summary: Player holds three fragments but the Monolith door does not accept them.
editorialAnalysis: Most reports come from fragments sitting in the stash rather than the inventory, or from arriving before the Precursor Fortress is raised. The insert prompt only appears with one of each type on your character and the Fortress revealed.
officialAnswer: Hold one of each fragment type in your inventory and travel to the Burning Monolith inside the revealed Fortress.

entries.question: Do I still need Calamity Fragments in 0.5?
summary: Player asks whether the old Calamity Fragment set is still the Arbiter key.
editorialAnalysis: As of 0.5.0 the Primary, Secondary and Tertiary Calamity Fragments can no longer be obtained; the Arbiter of Ash now uses the three Crisis Fragments. Any Calamity Fragments in your stash are legacy items.
officialAnswer: No - Calamity Fragments are disabled in 0.5; use Ancient, Faded and Weathered Crisis Fragments instead.

entries.question: Does Arbiter of Divinity also use these three fragments?
summary: Player wonders if the same Crisis Fragments open both Arbiters.
editorialAnalysis: Arbiter of Divinity is a separate 0.5 pinnacle reached through the Origins of Divinity arc and its own two new Citadels. It does NOT share the Crisis Fragment keys with the Arbiter of Ash.
officialAnswer: No - Arbiter of Divinity has its own key path; keep the three Crisis Fragments for the Arbiter of Ash.

directAnswer: The Precursor Fortress is not raised yet. Complete your first Tower to reveal it; the Burning Monolith then appears near the Atlas centre.
checks: Clear a Tower and re-open the Atlas to locate the Burning Monolith.

problems.symptom: Door will not accept my fragments
directAnswer: You likely hold duplicates of one type, or the fragments are in your stash. The door needs one of each type on your character.
checks: Confirm Ancient + Faded + Weathered are all in your inventory before travelling.

problems.symptom: First kill only needed two fragments
directAnswer: That is expected: on the first visit one key is pre-inserted and the other two come from the Western and Eastern Enigma Chambers. Repeat kills require a full Citadel farm of all three.
checks: For later kills, clear Iron, Copper and Stone Citadels for a complete set.
